big_case.notes: Challenges to how the federal judiciary adjudicates internal workplace sexual harassment and discrimination complaints carry genuine institutional sensitivity—reflected here in the recusal of the entire Fourth Circuit, a 127-page post-trial district court opinion, an amicus filing by legal accountability groups, and the Court's call for a response after an initial government waiver. At the same time, the substantive reach is confined to internal judicial-branch employment governance, the 2013 Fourth Circuit EDR Plan at issue had already been superseded, both questions presented suffered from severe preservation defects below, and the petition ended in a routine, unremarked certiorari denial without relist or separate statement.

leakage.notes: Forward prediction placed on 2026-10-29, eighteen days before the 2026-11-16 denial order. In retrieval_log.json (coverage 0.9; 36 captured calls and 4 unobserved web-search calls), the captured calls read only provisioned case inputs, schemas, statpack files, and 3 unrelated pre-2025 denied cert priors, while the 4 unobserved web-search queries sought general legal authorities (Supreme Court Rule 10 and 2 U.S.C. 1434) and never queried this case or its disposition.
